critique: The note proves conditional odd-factor transfer identification, even-factor nonidentification, finite-sample branch-free coverage, and regular full-frequency Wald inference, but all positive identification remains confined to a supplied causal order, known sampling factor, fixed dimension, and separation on a recursively defined coordinate set. The description of that set as “sharp” or “exact” exceeds the proved result: minimality is established only for closure under the chosen formal remainder recursion, not among all identification arguments using the joint transition and covariance equations. The total-certificate theorem also depends on the unproved CAD decision-and-sampling lemma, which is presented without the precise classical citation required to validate exact sampling over arbitrary effective real closed fields and open semialgebraic sets. The adaptive-calibration results merely reproduce the deterministic box with identical widths, so they add no adaptive inference result despite occupying headline-level space. These scope restrictions, the unsupported CAD leaf, and the absence of an implemented certificate or substantive application keep the projected leading-journal score below the strongest field-level examples. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
